app.envHint: Choose “Production” to run the booth. “Development” and “Staging” are meant for working on the application.

app.nameHint: Shown in the interface. Leave empty to use the built-in name.

camera.analogueGainHint: Sets the signal gain of the sensor. Higher values brighten the image and add noise, 0 adjusts the gain automatically.
camera.aspectRatioHint: Capture and preview must have the same aspect ratio. While the lock is closed, changing one dimension adjusts the other.
camera.autofocusModeHint: Only for cameras with a focus motor, such as the Camera Module 3. Keep “Default” for cameras without one, such as the HQ Camera.
camera.denoiseHint: Reduces the noise that becomes visible at a high gain. “Automatic” uses a fast reduction for the preview and a thorough one for the photos.
camera.exposureCompensationHint: Brightens (positive) or darkens (negative) the automatic exposure in stops. Has no effect if both exposure time and gain are fixed.
camera.exposureModeHint: Only applies to an automatic exposure time. “Short” keeps the exposure time short and raises the gain earlier, so moving guests stay sharper at the cost of a little more noise.
camera.exposureTimeHint: “Automatic” chooses exposure time and gain itself and in dim light exposes long enough to blur moving guests. A short fixed time such as 1/125 s keeps them sharp, but in a dark venue the image gets darker and noisier.
camera.flipHint: Mirrors the preview and the photos, for example for a camera behind a mirror.
camera.jpegQualityHint: Quality of the photos from 1 to 100. Higher values keep more detail and produce larger files.
camera.overlayLibraryHint: PNG files that are scaled to the size of each photo and drawn over it. A file with an existing name replaces the stored one, a download returns it as it is stored, deleting removes it from the storage right away.
camera.overlayPathHint: Overlay drawn over every photo. The choices are the PNG files of the overlay library below.
camera.previewFpsHint: Frames per second of the live preview. A lower framerate leaves more processing power for the photos, 15 suffice for the kiosk screen.
camera.rotationHint: Turns the preview and the photos upside down, for a camera mounted upside down. The sensor only supports 0° and 180°.
camera.sourceHint: “Webcam” takes the photos with the camera of the device whose browser shows the capture screen, “rpicam” with the Raspberry Pi camera. “gphoto2” controls a camera connected by USB, whose image size and exposure are set on the camera itself.
camera.whiteBalanceHint: Adjusts the colors to the light of the venue. “Automatic” suits most venues.

capture.adminEmailHint: Shown to a guest with their run number when emailing their photos fails. Leave empty to show a generic error message.
capture.eventNameHint: Appears in the emails to guests and in the caption of the layouts. The photos are stored in a folder named after the event.
capture.filePrefixHint: Start of the file names of the stored photos.
capture.saveOriginalsHint: Also stores a copy of each photo without the overlay while an overlay is active. Guests never receive these originals, the gallery can show and download them.
capture.welcomeMessageHint: Heading of the welcome screen. Leave empty to use the default greeting.

guide.importExport: Download saves the layout with all unsaved changes as a JSON file. Import opens such a file as a new layout. Saving it replaces a layout with the same ID.
guide.intro: The layout editor arranges the photos of a run on the paper of the printer. Positions and sizes are in millimeters of the paper, so the print matches the editor.
guide.layouts: A layout arranges the photos of a run in slots on the paper of the printer, in the order they were taken and with an optional caption. The print settings choose which layout is printed and shared.

shortcuts.alt: Hold while moving to duplicate the slots, while resizing to scale from the center
shortcuts.lock: Lock or unlock the selected slots
shortcuts.nudge: Move the selected slots by 1 millimeter
shortcuts.nudgeLarge: Move the selected slots by 10 millimeters
shortcuts.selectSlot: Select a slot of the page
shortcuts.shiftResize: Hold while resizing to keep the ratio
shortcuts.shiftSelect: Click with Shift, Ctrl, or Cmd held to add a slot to the selection or remove it. Drag on the empty canvas to select every unlocked slot it touches.

steps.1: Choose a layout or create a new one, and give it a name.
steps.2: Set the paper size to the paper of the printer, or choose one of the common sizes.
steps.3: Add a slot for every photo. Drag a slot to move it and its corners to resize it, or enter exact millimeters in the settings beside the canvas.
steps.4: Add pages if a run takes more photos than one page holds. A run continues on the next page once the slots of one are filled.
steps.5: Turn on the caption to print the name of the event and the date, and drag it to its place on the page.
steps.6: Save, then choose the layout in the print settings.

guide.view:
These aids only exist in the editor and are not part of the layout.

The grid shows steps of 10 millimeters, the rulers show millimeters on the paper, and lines show the coordinates of the pointer while dragging. With magnets, dragged slots snap onto the edges and centers of the other slots and of the paper, and a line shows the alignment. Holding Ctrl or Cmd places freely. While resizing, a loupe magnifies the area around the corner, which the toolbar can switch off. A click on a ruler places a guide across it that follows a drag: the top ruler places vertical guides, the left one horizontal guides. Slots snap to guides. A guide disappears when it is dragged back onto the ruler or double-clicked, all of them through the eraser in the toolbar. While moving, lines with measures show the distances to the neighbors, and even distances snap.

The preview shows the page as printed and keeps the slots above it editable. The view mode shows the page as printed and without the aids.

A sample photo appears in every slot the way the print crops it: from the center to the aspect ratio of the slot. It is kept in this browser for each saved layout, never uploaded, and never printed. Its opacity can be set in the toolbar.

A locked slot cannot be moved or resized and is skipped by the selection rectangle and the alignment. The align menu lines up the selected slots at an edge or a center line, or spaces them evenly. A single slot is aligned with the paper.

The list of the slots shows the order in which the photos of a run fill them. Dragging changes the order, the eye hides a slot for editing, the lock locks it. With several slots selected, position and size move and scale them together.
